wet_adhesion_surface_energetics.marine_relevance: Wet-adhesion loss / cathodic disbondment is the #1 field failure mode of marine anti-corrosion epoxy-amine coatings. This increment gives a parameter-free, non-circular directional ranking for it and PROVES it is a separate design axis from osmotic blistering -- correcting any single 'hydrophilicity' shortcut in the founder report.
wet_adhesion_surface_energetics.parameter_free_engine: Young-Dupre W_a(water) = gamma_water*(1+cos theta); zero fitted parameters
wet_adhesion_surface_energetics.relation_to_prior_receipts: The signed OWK receipt computed W_a(water)=107.2 for EP-DDS ONLY and did NOT compute EP-CYDM or EP-8CH2DA, the a-priori predictor, or the surface/bulk decoupling. W_a(DDS) reproduces here (107.235 mN/m) as a consistency check. This increment adds the other two networks, the non-circular predictor test, and the decoupling finding.
wet_adhesion_surface_energetics.target_capability: wet-adhesion-loss / cathodic-disbondment risk ranking of cured DGEBA-amine films
wet_adhesion_surface_energetics.theory: Cathodic disbondment / wet-adhesion loss is initiated when water thermodynamically displaces the coating<->steel bond at the buried interface. The parameter-free Young-Dupre work of water adhesion W_a(water) = gamma_water*(1+cos theta) measures the surface water-wetting driving force; a higher W_a(water) implies a more water-wettable surface and a larger disbondment driving force. This is a SURFACE property, physically distinct from BULK equilibrium uptake (which drives osmotic blistering and is free-volume-limited).
wet_adhesion_surface_energetics.verdict: WET_ADHESION_SURFACE_ENERGETICS__DIRECTION_VALIDATED_AND_DECOUPLED_FROM_BULK: the a-priori total-polar-atom density c_polar ranks SURFACE water wettability perfectly in-family (Spearman +1.0, n=3) and cross-class (Spearman 1.00), while the SAME descriptor ANTI-ranks BULK uptake (-0.5) and surface wettability itself ANTI-correlates with bulk uptake (-0.5). Surface (cathodic-disbondment) and bulk (osmotic-blistering) are governed by DIFFERENT physics -- polar-group chemistry vs free volume. The hydroxyl-only descriptor c_OH is the wrong surface descriptor (-0.5) because DDS's surface polarity is the sulfone, captured only by c_polar. NOT promotable: n=3 (not significant) and single-probe-liquid W_a(water) is not the full surface-energy split (needs >=2 probe liquids, protocol-controlled n>=~10). Actionable: rank disbondment risk by SURFACE polar-group density, blistering risk by FREE VOLUME; do not conflate.
